  command : ddflow pins regenerate [--only NAME] --approval request|ID
  item    : -    target: -
  acts on : the pin files as recorded before the re-record
  digest  : e00d0bdbb33adedc  (the state is read again when the agent runs it)

  args    : only=
  agent's reason (untrusted, not part of the approval): ""

data.claim: No: the lease object keeps the worktree and branch, but no event names a restore condition, so nothing can derive RESUME-READY.
data.falsifier: git grep finds a park or restore-condition event kind on main.
data.mechanism: The break, expire and forced-release paths append only lease.expired or lease.released; no event kind or fold carries a restore condition.
data.probe: git grep -c "lane.parked" main -- ddflow
data.probe_output: (no matches, exit 1 from git grep; the shell echo printed 0 for head)
data.question: Does a lease that ends with a worktree (break, expiry, forced release) leave any record of why and what restores it on main today?

evidence.note: R7cbeaff3f0 CONFIRMED: git grep lane.parked on main finds nothing; park record is new
Rules reviewed via brief guidance: knobs declared with docs and upgrade notes, fenced data in briefs, bounded lists (MAX_LISTED), log is the state (park derived, no second store), files under 20 KB
tests/test_park_and_resume.py 19 tests pass; fold, restore conditions, break parks for waiter, derived brief, hostile reason fenced, discard needs reason

chunk_findings.detail: `lanes resume <parked item>` always reports `eligible: True` and emits a `ddflow claim <item>` command, regardless of the park's restore condition. The function already obtains parked queue statuses (`PK.queue`) that carry `standing`/`why`, but the resume branch ignores them and only checks membership in `PK.parked_of(st)`. Given a lane parked with a future `time:` restore (or any restore condition that has not yet been met), the item is still parked, so this view tells the caller it is eligible to claim even though the restore condition should prevent resume. Eligibility should be derived from the parked row/status, not hardcoded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lane_views.py:_parked_view

chunk_findings.detail: The string fields are converted with `str(d.get("field", ""))`, which only handles a missing key; an explicit `None` value is stringified to `"None"`. For example, a `lane.resumed` event whose data contains `{"reason": None}` sets `closed_why="None"` instead of an empty reason, and a `lane.parked` event with a restore table like `{"kind": "at", "at": None}` stores `restore["at"] == "None"`, so any later clock/restore logic sees a bogus timestamp rather than an absent one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/parking.py (`h_parked`, `_restore`, `_close`)

chunk_findings.detail: The park is performed as a separate step after the lease-end event has already been appended. If `PK.park_lease` fails (e.g. raises the new `ParkError` from `services/parking.py`) or the process dies after `log.append(kind, item_id, payload(lease))` but before the `lane.parked` append completes, the lease-end event (`lane.expired` or `lane.released`) is already in the log while no `lane.parked` is recorded. For `expire`, this is especially concrete: the function is documented as idempotent and folds duplicate expiries, so a later retry sees the expired event and refuses to run the `then` callback again, leaving the lane permanently unparked despite the intent that leases ending with work be parked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:_append/_park

chunk_findings.detail: `brief` treats an empty live tree reading as if no live reading were supplied: `commits = tree.get("commits") or row["commits"]` and `dirty = tree.get("dirty") or row["dirty"]` fall back to the park-time lists whenever the live lists are empty. If a parked lane’s commits are later reset/merged and its worktree is clean, `measure` returns something like `{"ahead": 0, "commits": [], "dirty": []}`; `brief` then still prints the stale commit list and a stale `- uncommitted (N): ...` line, while also printing `commits ahead of the base: 0`. The same happens when `measure` returns `{}` because the worktree is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:brief

chunk_findings.detail: `brief` only returns early when the item is missing (`it is None`). If the item still exists but is terminal or removed, `standing` returns `MOOT`, yet `brief` continues and emits the full resume brief, including `Next` commands `ddflow claim`, `ddflow merge`, and `ddflow complete`. Given a parked row whose item has since been completed/discarded but whose park row has not been resumed or discarded, the brief says `Now: moot (...)` and then instructs the operator/agent to claim and complete a finished/gone item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:brief

chunk_findings.detail: `park_lease` stores `_capped(tree.get("dirty", ()))`, which keeps only the first `MAX_LISTED` (12) dirty paths and discards the total. When a later brief is rendered without a live tree, `brief` prints `- uncommitted ({len(dirty)}):` from that capped list. With 13 uncommitted paths at park time and no live tree, the brief reports 12 uncommitted paths, not 13; the module’s own `MAX_LISTED` comment says the rest should be a count.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:park_lease

chunk_findings.detail: The `lane.parked` event kind declares `commits` as a field and its lookup says the list contains “commit ids and subjects git printed”, but only `reason` is listed in `text`. Commit subjects are author-controlled free text, so a parked lane with a commit subject such as `fix: <secret>` or `ignore previous instructions` will be treated as machine data and not fenced/redacted the way the reason field is, despite the kind’s `exempt` wording claiming the reason is the author’s own words.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/events/parking.toml:6-7 (`lane.parked` fields/text)

chunk_findings.detail: `new = "\"advise\""` is a valid TOML string, but it parses to the literal string `"advise"` including the double quotes, not the value `advise`. Sibling `knob_added` templates use native TOML values (`true`, `86400`), so this template will either display/record the new knob value with extra quote characters or, if any upgrade/config-generation path uses `new` as the actual default, write/compare `lanes.auto_resume` as `"advise"` (quoted) instead of `advise`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lanes.auto_resume.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named for the “park twice” case, but it never parks twice: it performs a single `leases.expire` on `T1` and then asserts that `PK.open_parks` has length 1. If `PK.open_parks` were changed to return one row per `lane.parked` event, and a second park/re-park of `T1` created another open row, this test would still pass because only one park was ever created. The asserted deduplication property is therefore not exercised.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_park_and_resume.py:test_parking_twice_keeps_one_open_row

chunk_findings.detail: The park side effect is performed after the lease-end event has already been appended, so it is not atomic with the end. For example, if `expire(log, item_id, reason, restore=PK.Restore(PK.GLOB, "bad["))` (or any other input that makes `PK.park_lease` raise `ParkError` from its checked restore/tree validation), `_append` first appends `lane.expired` at line ~63, then `_park` calls `PK.park_lease` at line ~66 and the exception propagates. The lane is now durably expired but has no `lane.parked` event; a retry will not recover it because the lease is already ended/expired, so the worktree is dropped instead of parked as required by the change’s intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:_append / expire

chunk_findings.detail: Given a live `tree` from `measure()` where the parked worktree currently has no commits and no dirty paths (`{"commits": [], "dirty": []}`), `brief()` uses `or` and treats those empty lists as missing, falling back to `row["commits"]` and `row["dirty"]` recorded when the lane was parked. If the commits were merged/reset or the dirty changes were cleaned after parking, the brief still lists the stale recorded commits/dirty paths as current work, even though the live tree says there is none.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:279

chunk_findings.detail: `brief()` only early-returns when `it is None`, but `standing()` also marks a row `MOOT` when the item exists and is `removed` or `terminal`. For a parked row whose item has since been completed by another lane (`it.terminal=True`), the brief still prints Objective, Remaining gates, Work attached, and the `## Next` commands telling the user to run `ddflow claim <item>`, `ddflow merge <item>`, and `ddflow complete <item>`, which is wrong because the item is already finished.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:265

chunk_findings.detail: For an `ITEM` restore condition, `standing()` treats the target as cleared only when it is missing, `terminal`, or has `merged_sha`; it does not check `t.removed`. If the target item is present in state as a tombstone with `removed=True` but not terminal/merged, `standing()` returns `WAITING` forever (“waits for … to merge”), even though the same function treats `removed` on the parked item itself as moot and a removed target cannot merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:180

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_person_park_ends_the_lease_and_keeps_the_tree` says the park “ends the lease,” but after invoking `lanes park` it only asserts the parked row’s cause and that the worktree still exists. It never checks that the lease is no longer live, e.g. `_state(repo).items["T1"].lease.live(time.time(), 0)` is false, nor that another agent can subsequently claim the item. A buggy `lanes park` implementation that records `lane.parked` while leaving the old lease live would pass this test unchanged, hiding a parked lane that still blocks new claims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_park_and_resume.py:207

chunk_findings.detail: The test named for “parking twice” actually parks once: it claims `T1`, calls `leases.expire(...)` once, and then asserts one open park. A buggy park/expire path that emits duplicate `lane.parked` rows on a second park (for example after the item is re-claimed and expired again) would pass unchanged because the second park is never exercised. The test does not enforce the one-open-row invariant it claims to test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_park_and_resume.py:77

chunk_findings.detail: The new operator bypass is too broad: it makes `eligible` true whenever the parked row’s `restore.kind` is `PK.OPERATOR`, even if the queue standing says the item is not resumable for another reason. For example, take a parked item whose restore kind is `operator` and whose item has since been completed or discarded. The parked row is still present and `PK.queue` still yields a standing for it with `ready=False` and a MOOT/not-ready `why` (the same condition used to justify the moot-brief fix). The expression `stand.ready or PK.parked_of(st)[item]["restore"]["kind"] == PK.OPERATOR` short-circuits to true, so `_parked_view` returns `eligible: True` and emits `ddflow claim <item>` for a terminal/moot item. The operator restore condition should not override a standing that says the item cannot be resumed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lane_views.py:_parked_view

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_capped` behavior appends a pseudo-row such as `(+2 more)` into the same list that callers still treat as the list of dirty paths/commits. Given a parked lane with 14 dirty paths and a brief rendered without a live tree reading, `_capped` returns 13 entries: the first 12 paths plus `(+2 more)`. The brief then uses `len(dirty)` for its `- uncommitted ({len(dirty)}):` line, so it reports 13 uncommitted paths instead of 14 and prints the marker as if it were another path. The count is only accidentally correct when the total is exactly `MAX_LISTED + 1`; for any larger total it under-reports the work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:_capped

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten value `new = '"advise"'` is still a TOML string whose parsed content is `"advise"` with literal double-quote characters, not the knob value `advise`. The change from `new = "\"advise\""` to `new = '"advise"'` is therefore a no-op semantically: both parse to the same quoted string. If the upgrade path uses the parsed `new` value as the default for `lanes.auto_resume`, comparisons to `advise` fail or the generated config records an extra layer of quoting, while sibling `knob_added` templates use native TOML values such as `true` and `86400`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lanes.auto_resume.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test checks `"lease.expired" not in _kinds(repo)`, but the lease-expire event kind in this codebase is `lane.expired` (the lease lifecycle appends `lane.expired` / `lane.released`, as reflected in the prior finding and the surrounding `lane.*` event naming). If `leases.expire` regresses to appending the lease-end event before validating the restore condition and then raising `PK.ParkError`, `_kinds(repo)` will contain `lane.expired`, not `lease.expired`, so the assertion still passes. The test therefore does not actually guard the “refuse before the lease ends” fix; it should assert that the real lease-end kind, e.g. `lane.expired`, is absent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_park_and_resume.py:test_a_bad_restore_condition_refuses_before_the_lease_ends

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lane_views.py:166

chunk_findings.detail: The new `t.removed` branch makes `standing()` report `READY` with the reason `"<target> has merged"` even when the target item was removed rather than merged. Given a parked lane whose restore condition is `{kind: ITEM, target: "T2"}` and state where `st.items["T2"].removed` is true but `terminal` and `merged_sha` are false, the function returns `READY` and the text `"T2 has merged"`. That is a false user-visible statement: the condition is cleared because the target is gone, not because it merged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:186

chunk_findings.detail: `lanes resume <parked item>` always reports `eligible: True` and emits a `ddflow claim <item>` command, regardless of the park's restore condition. The function already obtains parked queue statuses (`PK.queue`) that carry `standing`/`why`, but the resume branch ignores them and only checks membership in `PK.parked_of(st)`. Given a lane parked with a future `time:` restore (or any restore condition that has not yet been met), the item is still parked, so this view tells the caller it is eligible to claim even though the restore condition should prevent resume. Eligibility should be derived from the parked row/status, not hardcoded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lane_views.py:_parked_view

chunk_findings.detail: The string fields are converted with `str(d.get("field", ""))`, which only handles a missing key; an explicit `None` value is stringified to `"None"`. For example, a `lane.resumed` event whose data contains `{"reason": None}` sets `closed_why="None"` instead of an empty reason, and a `lane.parked` event with a restore table like `{"kind": "at", "at": None}` stores `restore["at"] == "None"`, so any later clock/restore logic sees a bogus timestamp rather than an absent one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/parking.py (`h_parked`, `_restore`, `_close`)

chunk_findings.detail: The park is performed as a separate step after the lease-end event has already been appended. If `PK.park_lease` fails (e.g. raises the new `ParkError` from `services/parking.py`) or the process dies after `log.append(kind, item_id, payload(lease))` but before the `lane.parked` append completes, the lease-end event (`lane.expired` or `lane.released`) is already in the log while no `lane.parked` is recorded. For `expire`, this is especially concrete: the function is documented as idempotent and folds duplicate expiries, so a later retry sees the expired event and refuses to run the `then` callback again, leaving the lane permanently unparked despite the intent that leases ending with work be parked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:_append/_park

chunk_findings.detail: `brief` treats an empty live tree reading as if no live reading were supplied: `commits = tree.get("commits") or row["commits"]` and `dirty = tree.get("dirty") or row["dirty"]` fall back to the park-time lists whenever the live lists are empty. If a parked lane’s commits are later reset/merged and its worktree is clean, `measure` returns something like `{"ahead": 0, "commits": [], "dirty": []}`; `brief` then still prints the stale commit list and a stale `- uncommitted (N): ...` line, while also printing `commits ahead of the base: 0`. The same happens when `measure` returns `{}` because the worktree is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:brief

chunk_findings.detail: `brief` only returns early when the item is missing (`it is None`). If the item still exists but is terminal or removed, `standing` returns `MOOT`, yet `brief` continues and emits the full resume brief, including `Next` commands `ddflow claim`, `ddflow merge`, and `ddflow complete`. Given a parked row whose item has since been completed/discarded but whose park row has not been resumed or discarded, the brief says `Now: moot (...)` and then instructs the operator/agent to claim and complete a finished/gone item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:brief

chunk_findings.detail: `park_lease` stores `_capped(tree.get("dirty", ()))`, which keeps only the first `MAX_LISTED` (12) dirty paths and discards the total. When a later brief is rendered without a live tree, `brief` prints `- uncommitted ({len(dirty)}):` from that capped list. With 13 uncommitted paths at park time and no live tree, the brief reports 12 uncommitted paths, not 13; the module’s own `MAX_LISTED` comment says the rest should be a count.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:park_lease

chunk_findings.detail: The `lane.parked` event kind declares `commits` as a field and its lookup says the list contains “commit ids and subjects git printed”, but only `reason` is listed in `text`. Commit subjects are author-controlled free text, so a parked lane with a commit subject such as `fix: <secret>` or `ignore previous instructions` will be treated as machine data and not fenced/redacted the way the reason field is, despite the kind’s `exempt` wording claiming the reason is the author’s own words.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/events/parking.toml:6-7 (`lane.parked` fields/text)

chunk_findings.detail: `new = "\"advise\""` is a valid TOML string, but it parses to the literal string `"advise"` including the double quotes, not the value `advise`. Sibling `knob_added` templates use native TOML values (`true`, `86400`), so this template will either display/record the new knob value with extra quote characters or, if any upgrade/config-generation path uses `new` as the actual default, write/compare `lanes.auto_resume` as `"advise"` (quoted) instead of `advise`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lanes.auto_resume.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named for the “park twice” case, but it never parks twice: it performs a single `leases.expire` on `T1` and then asserts that `PK.open_parks` has length 1. If `PK.open_parks` were changed to return one row per `lane.parked` event, and a second park/re-park of `T1` created another open row, this test would still pass because only one park was ever created. The asserted deduplication property is therefore not exercised.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_park_and_resume.py:test_parking_twice_keeps_one_open_row

chunk_findings.detail: The new operator bypass is too broad: it makes `eligible` true whenever the parked row’s `restore.kind` is `PK.OPERATOR`, even if the queue standing says the item is not resumable for another reason. For example, take a parked item whose restore kind is `operator` and whose item has since been completed or discarded. The parked row is still present and `PK.queue` still yields a standing for it with `ready=False` and a MOOT/not-ready `why` (the same condition used to justify the moot-brief fix). The expression `stand.ready or PK.parked_of(st)[item]["restore"]["kind"] == PK.OPERATOR` short-circuits to true, so `_parked_view` returns `eligible: True` and emits `ddflow claim <item>` for a terminal/moot item. The operator restore condition should not override a standing that says the item cannot be resumed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lane_views.py:_parked_view

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_capped` behavior appends a pseudo-row such as `(+2 more)` into the same list that callers still treat as the list of dirty paths/commits. Given a parked lane with 14 dirty paths and a brief rendered without a live tree reading, `_capped` returns 13 entries: the first 12 paths plus `(+2 more)`. The brief then uses `len(dirty)` for its `- uncommitted ({len(dirty)}):` line, so it reports 13 uncommitted paths instead of 14 and prints the marker as if it were another path. The count is only accidentally correct when the total is exactly `MAX_LISTED + 1`; for any larger total it under-reports the work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:_capped

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten value `new = '"advise"'` is still a TOML string whose parsed content is `"advise"` with literal double-quote characters, not the knob value `advise`. The change from `new = "\"advise\""` to `new = '"advise"'` is therefore a no-op semantically: both parse to the same quoted string. If the upgrade path uses the parsed `new` value as the default for `lanes.auto_resume`, comparisons to `advise` fail or the generated config records an extra layer of quoting, while sibling `knob_added` templates use native TOML values such as `true` and `86400`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lanes.auto_resume.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test checks `"lease.expired" not in _kinds(repo)`, but the lease-expire event kind in this codebase is `lane.expired` (the lease lifecycle appends `lane.expired` / `lane.released`, as reflected in the prior finding and the surrounding `lane.*` event naming). If `leases.expire` regresses to appending the lease-end event before validating the restore condition and then raising `PK.ParkError`, `_kinds(repo)` will contain `lane.expired`, not `lease.expired`, so the assertion still passes. The test therefore does not actually guard the “refuse before the lease ends” fix; it should assert that the real lease-end kind, e.g. `lane.expired`, is absent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_park_and_resume.py:test_a_bad_restore_condition_refuses_before_the_lease_ends

chunk_findings.detail: The park side effect is performed after the lease-end event has already been appended, so it is not atomic with the end. For example, if `expire(log, item_id, reason, restore=PK.Restore(PK.GLOB, "bad["))` (or any other input that makes `PK.park_lease` raise `ParkError` from its checked restore/tree validation), `_append` first appends `lane.expired` at line ~63, then `_park` calls `PK.park_lease` at line ~66 and the exception propagates. The lane is now durably expired but has no `lane.parked` event; a retry will not recover it because the lease is already ended/expired, so the worktree is dropped instead of parked as required by the change’s intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:_append / expire

chunk_findings.detail: Given a live `tree` from `measure()` where the parked worktree currently has no commits and no dirty paths (`{"commits": [], "dirty": []}`), `brief()` uses `or` and treats those empty lists as missing, falling back to `row["commits"]` and `row["dirty"]` recorded when the lane was parked. If the commits were merged/reset or the dirty changes were cleaned after parking, the brief still lists the stale recorded commits/dirty paths as current work, even though the live tree says there is none.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:279

chunk_findings.detail: `brief()` only early-returns when `it is None`, but `standing()` also marks a row `MOOT` when the item exists and is `removed` or `terminal`. For a parked row whose item has since been completed by another lane (`it.terminal=True`), the brief still prints Objective, Remaining gates, Work attached, and the `## Next` commands telling the user to run `ddflow claim <item>`, `ddflow merge <item>`, and `ddflow complete <item>`, which is wrong because the item is already finished.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:265

chunk_findings.detail: For an `ITEM` restore condition, `standing()` treats the target as cleared only when it is missing, `terminal`, or has `merged_sha`; it does not check `t.removed`. If the target item is present in state as a tombstone with `removed=True` but not terminal/merged, `standing()` returns `WAITING` forever (“waits for … to merge”), even though the same function treats `removed` on the parked item itself as moot and a removed target cannot merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:180

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_person_park_ends_the_lease_and_keeps_the_tree` says the park “ends the lease,” but after invoking `lanes park` it only asserts the parked row’s cause and that the worktree still exists. It never checks that the lease is no longer live, e.g. `_state(repo).items["T1"].lease.live(time.time(), 0)` is false, nor that another agent can subsequently claim the item. A buggy `lanes park` implementation that records `lane.parked` while leaving the old lease live would pass this test unchanged, hiding a parked lane that still blocks new claims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_park_and_resume.py:207

chunk_findings.detail: The test named for “parking twice” actually parks once: it claims `T1`, calls `leases.expire(...)` once, and then asserts one open park. A buggy park/expire path that emits duplicate `lane.parked` rows on a second park (for example after the item is re-claimed and expired again) would pass unchanged because the second park is never exercised. The test does not enforce the one-open-row invariant it claims to test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_park_and_resume.py:77

chunk_findings.detail: The new resume eligibility treats any parked row whose restore condition is `OPERATOR` as eligible whenever a standing row exists, even when that standing row is not actually resumable. For example, if a lane was parked with `restore.kind == PK.OPERATOR` and the item has since been completed or removed, `standing()` marks the row MOOT/not ready (`stand.ready` false, `stand.why` explaining the moot condition), but the `or` clause still makes `resume.eligible` true and returns `command: "ddflow claim <item>"`. That re-offers a claim/resume command for a terminal or removed item, which is wrong because the item cannot be claimed again.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lane_views.py:166

chunk_findings.detail: The new `t.removed` branch makes `standing()` report `READY` with the reason `"<target> has merged"` even when the target item was removed rather than merged. Given a parked lane whose restore condition is `{kind: ITEM, target: "T2"}` and state where `st.items["T2"].removed` is true but `terminal` and `merged_sha` are false, the function returns `READY` and the text `"T2 has merged"`. That is a false user-visible statement: the condition is cleared because the target is gone, not because it merged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:186

chunk_findings.detail: The new uncommitted-brief line drops the `MAX_LISTED` truncation that the previous code applied (`dirty[:MAX_LISTED]`). Given a parked lane whose `dirty` list has more than `MAX_LISTED` paths, the brief now emits every uncommitted path in a single comma-separated line, while the commit list above it remains capped. This defeats the existing bounded-list behavior for the brief and can produce an arbitrarily long uncommitted line; removing the count did not require removing the `MAX_LISTED` cap.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parking.py:297

data.body:
R-mode-parity 5 (start now). A test that no MCP or CLI --json body lacks a schema id and version, covering bare arrays (view progress) and markdown-only views (board); required by r-external-frontends. SIZE M, RISK low. FALSIFIER: view progress still returns an untagged array. CONFORMANCE (r-mode-parity, r-surface-budget, r-log-is-the-state, r-external-frontends, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-upgrade-safe, r-untrusted-data, r-consent-outward, r-secrets, r-evidence-over-assertion, r-everything-configurable, r-docs-with-the-change, D-mode-parity-answers, D-external-frontends, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-mode-parity): one registry feeds every mode; a command unavailable in a mode has a recorded reason and a fallback; results are bounded and carry a schema id; no GUI; no second store.

OPERATOR DECISION 2026-11-12: additive envelope. Bare-array --json bodies (progress, loops, ...) stay bare by default (D-compat, ARRAY_PAYLOADS unchanged, no schema_versions bump). Opt-in knob [output].json_envelope answers {schema, rows} instead. Test: tests/test_schema_ids_all.py (default stays an array; opt-in carries schema id and version; object, refusal and MCP bodies unchanged).

data.consequences: Callers that need a tag opt in per project; default consumers are unaffected.
data.context: MP-schema-all falsifier: view progress returned an untagged array; D-compat keeps arrays bare.
data.decision: Bare-array bodies stay bare by default (D-compat, ARRAY_PAYLOADS unchanged). [output].json_envelope = true answers {schema, rows} so every --json body can carry a schema id and version. No schema version is bumped.
data.title: Bare-array --json bodies get an additive opt-in schema envelope

chunk_findings.detail: The test promises that an enveloped array body carries a command-specific schema id of the form `<command>@<n>`, but it only asserts that the schema string is non-empty and that the part after `@` is all digits. If the implementation returns a generic schema id such as `"array@1"` for every array command, both parametrized cases still pass. Thus a regression that drops the command identity from the schema id is not caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_schema_ids_all.py:test_with_the_envelope_on_every_array_carries_a_schema_id_and_version

chunk_findings.detail: The intent and test name say object bodies are unchanged when `[output].json_envelope` is enabled, but the test compares only the `schema` field before and after enabling the envelope. If the implementation changes the object body in any other way while preserving `schema` — for example by adding a `rows` key, adding envelope metadata, or mutating another field — this test still passes. The assertion does not keep the stated D-compat promise for objects.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_schema_ids_all.py:test_an_object_body_is_the_same_with_the_envelope_on

chunk_findings.detail: The test only checks that a refusal body contains `refusal` and does not contain `rows`. A refusal body that has been altered by the envelope logic but still contains `refusal` and lacks `rows`, for example by gaining a `schema` key or other envelope metadata, would pass. The test therefore does not actually verify that refusals are unchanged, only that they are not wrapped in the specific `rows` shape.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_schema_ids_all.py:test_a_refusal_body_is_never_wrapped

data.body:
Fixes bug B4b7b99ecec: Order-dependent: 'section zz is declared twice (test_compat_aliases and test_compat_aliases)' appears in full-suite runs and in two-file runs on primary main, and passes when run alone; the ci gate counts it as a new failure on any branch. Found on MP-schema-all.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B4b7b99ecec --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B4b7b99ecec --regression-test <test>` first).

Not attached, they match nothing in the tree: tests/test_schema_ids_all.py, ddflow/surfaces/schemas_registry.py, ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.output.json_envelope.toml.
